name: Jehukal
title: King Zedekiah's Envoy
summary: Jehukal (also called Jucal) was the son of Shelemiah and one of the officials at King Zedekiah's court in Judah. He was sent by the king to ask the prophet Jeremiah to pray for the people, but later he was among the princes who demanded Jeremiah's death because the prophet's message was considered demoralizing for the defense of Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: Sent as a Messenger to Jeremiah
keyEvents.description: King Zedekiah sent Jehukal (Jucal) along with the priest Shephatiah to the prophet Jeremiah to ask him to pray to the Lord for the people under the Babylonian threat.

keyEvents.title: Demanded Jeremiah's Death
keyEvents.description: Jehukal was among the princes who heard Jeremiah's prophecies that Jerusalem would fall to the Babylonians, and they demanded that the king put the prophet to death because his words weakened morale among the soldiers and the people.

keyEvents.title: Jeremiah Thrown into the Cistern
keyEvents.description: As a result of the demands from Jehucal and the other princes, Jeremiah was thrown into Malkijah's cistern where he sank into the mud, in an attempt to silence him.

keyEvents.title: Archaeological confirmation – the bulla discovery
keyEvents.description: In 2005, a seal impression (bulla) was found in excavations at the City of David in Jerusalem with the inscription "belonging to Jehucal son of Shelemijah son of Shobi," confirming the historical existence of this biblical figure.

keyEvents.title: The conflict between the princes and Jeremiah
keyEvents.description: Jehucal represented the political faction at court that opposed Jeremiah's message of submission to Babylon. This conflict illustrates the tension between political power and prophetic authority in Judah's final days.
